text.p: Pakistan on Monday announced schedule details for the February 3 elections of the National Assembly (lower house) and four provincial assemblies.
President Farooq Leghari set the date after he sacked Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule and dissolved the National Assembly on November 5.
"This is the first time that it has been decided to hold national and provincial elections on the same day," Chief Election Commissioner Sardar Fakhr Alam said on television.
"It will save election expenses of the government as well as of the candidates and save a holiday," he said, adding that 28 of Pakistan's 33 political parties supported the decision.
Alam said residents of the semi-autonomous Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) bordering Afghanistan would be able to vote in the general elections for the first time.
Previously, voting rights in FATA were restricted to a few thousand tribal chiefs, who elected eight National Assembly members who in turn elected eight Senators.
Alam said that nomination papers will be received from December 17 to 21 and reviewed from December 26 to 28.
Appeals against rejection or acceptance of nominations must be filed by December 31 and will be heard by January 7. Candidates can withdraw their papers up to January 8.
The final list of candidates will be published on January 9.

Alam said candidates could not fly banners, use hoardings or write slogans on walls during the campaign. No party flags would be allowed on government buildings and no loud-speakers used, except at rallies. Violators faced a year in jail or a fine, he said.
Vote-counting would take place at polling stations, where results would be announced.
He said a code of conduct on campaigning by political parties had been prepared, but gave no details.
"I appeal to the voters to cooperate with the Election Commission for the holding of peaceful elections in accordance with true democratic traditions," Alam said.
Alam said the people should elect honest, sincere, patriotic and Islamic-minded people.
"The vote is a weapon which, properly used, can give this country a good democratic government.

"The survival of Pakistan is linked with democracy and stability of democratic institutions, and the holding of free, fair and transparent elections is the first brick of this foundation," he declared.
Pakistan, with an estimated population of 131 million, has 52.32 million registered voters. Turnout has averaged 40 to 45 percent in the last three general elections.
